fact_en: Solid modeling clay can be molded into new shapes! It remains a solid because its definite volume does not change.
fact_bis: Ang solid modeling clay pwede hubaron og bag-ong shapes! Magpabilin kini nga solid kay dili mausab ang iyang definite volume.

findings.note: Tagalog false friend. title_bis "Clay Hubog Solid Pareho" for EN "Clay Molds Solid": Tagalog hubog = shape/mold, but Cebuano hubog = DRUNK. The body repeats the error with a different wrong word — "pwede hubaron og bag-ong shapes" (Cebuano hubad/hubaron = to untie, undress, translate), not hulmahon/hulmahan. The card's only fact is that clay can be MOLDED into new shapes while staying solid, and the word carrying it is wrong in both the headline and the body, never corrected.

fact_en: When iron nails are left in the rain, they react with oxygen to form a new substance called rust!
fact_bis: Kung ibutang ang mga pako nga puthaw sa ulan, mo-react kini sa oxygen ug mahimong bag-ong substance nga kalawang!

findings.note: Title 'Pako sa Ulan Kalawang' and body 'mga pako nga puthaw' render English 'iron nails' as pako, which in Cebuano means WING/fin (nail = lansang). Tagalog false friend; the card never says lansang, so a child reads 'iron wings left in the rain turn to rust' and the object of the rust fact is a different thing throughout. Corpus confirms the correct word: ffct-15177/16425/28301 all use lansang for the same nails.

fact_en: Heating a sealed aerosol spray can increases the gas pressure inside, which can cause the metal container to explode!
fact_bis: Kung painiton ang sealed nga aerosol spray can, mosaka ang gas pressure sa sulod, nga makapahugno sa metal nga container!

findings.note: Safety card: English says heating a sealed aerosol can raises internal pressure and can make the metal container EXPLODE (mobuto). Cebuano says 'makapahugno sa metal nga container' — hugno means COLLAPSE/cave in, the opposite direction of a pressure burst (the corpus uses hugno correctly for a collapsing cave roof, ffct-29695). The title 'Aerosol Init Pressure Puto' offers no correction — puto is a rice cake in Cebuano (explosion = buto/pabuto), so the burst fact is nowhere in the Cebuano card.

fact_en:
Ever wonder what makes the West Philippine Sea so salty?

It's a homogeneous mixture! The sodium chloride dissolves completely in the liquid water, making it perfectly mixed.
fact_bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo ngano nga asalom kaayo ang West Philippine Sea?

Kini usa ka homogeneous mixture! Ang sodium chloride nag-dissolve gyud sa liquid water, mao nga perpekto ang sagol.

findings.note: English asks why the West Philippine Sea is so SALTY; Cebuano asks 'ngano nga asalom kaayo ang West Philippine Sea' — aslom/asalom means SOUR, not salty (salty = parat). Nothing in the Cebuano restores it: the only corrective is the English term 'sodium chloride', which a grade-5 reader will not map to asin. The child ends up believing seawater is sour. Corpus usage confirms the split: aslom is used 109x for sour (calamansi, lactic acid) and parat 224x for salty.

title_bis: Metal nga Tulay Nagtapak sa Init
fact_en:
What happens to a metal bridge on a hot, sunny day?

Heating it makes its metal particles move faster and spread slightly apart, making the solid structure expand!
fact_bis:
Unsay mahitabo sa metal nga tulay sa init nga adlaw?

Kung initon kini, ang mga particle sa metal molihok ug mas paspas ug mag-spread gamay, mao nga mo-expand ang solid nga istruktura!

findings.note: title_bis "Metal nga Tulay Nagtapak sa Init" for "Metal Bridges Expand in Heat": tapak in Cebuano is to step on / to patch, not to expand. The headline a child sees says the bridge steps on the heat, which names a different action entirely (Cebuano for expand is molapad/modako/mobuka). Corpus-wide, this same mis-mapping shows up in ~10 other titles for expand/spread (ffct-19997 "Nagtapak nga Hangin", ffct-21565 "Yelo Nagtapak Molutaw", ffct-15395 "Kalayo sa Pagkatapak", etc.), so it is a systematic title-generation defect, not one-off awkwardness.

fact_en:
Why does water expand when it freezes into ice?

When liquid water freezes into solid ice, it expands by about 9 percent in volume, making ice less dense than water!
fact_bis:
Nganong mo-expand ang tubig kung mo-freeze?

Kung ang liquid water mo-freeze ngadto sa solid ice, mo-expand siya mga 9 percent sa volume, mao nga ang ice mas dili dense kaysa sa tubig!

findings.note: title_bis "Yelo 9 Porsiyento Pagtapak" for "Ice Expands 9 Percent": same tapak (step on / patch) used for expand, leaving the headline as "Ice 9 Percent Stepping" - the whole point of the card (ice expands ~9% on freezing) is absent from the title and replaced by a different action.

fact_en: Ice left outside on a hot sunny day in Manila melts into liquid water because heat increases molecular motion!
fact_bis: Ang yelo sa gawas sa init nga adlaw sa Manila matunaw ngadto sa liquid water kay ang kainit nagpadaghan sa lihok sa mga molekula!

findings.note: title_bis "Namatyan nga Yelo sa Manila" for "Melting Ice in Manila". `namatyan` means bereaved / had someone die on it, not melted (natunaw, which the body uses). The headline reads "Bereaved Ice in Manila" — a different word entirely, not a compactness or register issue.

fact_en: The metal pot used to cook sinigang has high thermal conductivity, meaning it transfers heat quickly!
fact_bis: Ang metal nga kaldero nga gigamit sa pagluto sa sinigang adunay taas nga thermal conductivity, pasabot dali kini makapasa og kainit!

findings.note: title_bis "Palayok Thermal Conductivity" for "Pot Thermal Conductivity". A palayok is an EARTHENWARE/clay pot (and a Tagalog word; Cebuano kolon) — the opposite of the card's subject, which the body correctly calls "metal nga kaldero" with HIGH thermal conductivity. The headline asserts a clay pot conducts heat quickly, which is false and is exactly the counterexample a grade-5 conductivity lesson uses.

fact_en: HEPA air filters trap solid dust particles and pollen from the indoor air gas mixture!
fact_bis: Ang HEPA air filters mopakpak sa solid dust particles ug pollen gikan sa indoor air gas mixture!

findings.note: Body: "Ang HEPA air filters mopakpak sa solid dust particles ug pollen…" — `pakpak` is a wing / to flap or clap in Cebuano, not to trap or catch (modakop / mosala). The trapping action is the card's only fact and no other word in the card supplies it; title_bis "Mga Filter sa HEPA" just repeats the English name.

fact_en:
What happens inside the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River cave?

Inside the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River, water vapor condenses into liquid droplets right on the cave walls!
fact_bis:
Unsay nahitabo sa sulod sa Puerto Princesa Subterranean River cave?

Sa Puerto Princesa Subterranean River, ang water vapor nag-condense ngadto sa liquid droplets sa cave walls!

findings.note: title_bis "Paghalay sa Langob" for title_en "Cave Condensation". Cebuano halay/ihalay = to hang out to DRY (laundry) — the headline says "Drying in the Cave", the opposite direction of the gas-to-liquid change the card teaches; in Tagalog reading it is worse (kahalayan). The sibling card ffct-20750, same subject, correctly titles it "Kondensasyon". The headline a child sees names the reverse process; only the body's English loanword "nag-condense" carries the real fact.

fact_en:
Why does a sealed glass water bottle shatter in the freezer?

Water expands when it freezes into solid ice! This expansion is why leaving a sealed glass bottle in the freezer can shatter the glass.
fact_bis:
Nganong mabali ang sealed nga botelya nga puno ug tubig sa freezer?

Mogawas ang tubig kung magyelo kini ug mahimong solid ice! Maong kung ibutang nimo ang sealed nga botelya sa freezer, basin mabali ang baso.

findings.note: Body + emph_bis. EN: "Water expands when it freezes into solid ice! This expansion is why leaving a sealed glass bottle in the freezer can shatter the glass." BIS: "Mogawas ang tubig kung magyelo kini..." = "the water COMES OUT when it freezes" (mogawas = to exit/go out; expand is mohabok/modako/mo-expand). The card's whole mechanism is expansion, and nothing else in the card restores it — the Cebuano instead states something physically false for a SEALED bottle (nothing can come out). The wrong word is the one tagged in emph_bis, so it is the highlighted takeaway. A child learns "freezing water leaks out of the bottle" instead of "ice takes up more space than water".

fact_en: When fallen narra tree leaves decompose in the soil, they undergo a chemical change to become nutrient-rich organic compost!
fact_bis: Kung mo-decompose ang mga nahulog nga dahon sa narra sa yuta, mahimong nutrient-rich organic compost kini!

findings.note: EN: "...they undergo a chemical change to become nutrient-rich organic compost!" BIS: "Kung mo-decompose ang mga nahulog nga dahon sa narra sa yuta, mahimong nutrient-rich organic compost kini!" — the phrase "chemical change" is dropped entirely (emph_bis is null, while every sibling card in this chemical-change set emphasises it, e.g. ffct-20731, ffct-20741, ffct-20755). What remains is common knowledge (leaves rot into compost); the card's only curriculum point — that decomposition classifies as a chemical change — is unrecoverable from the Cebuano, so a child cannot answer "anong klase nga pagbag-o ang pagkadunot?"
